case: A capability declares a consequence term the mapping table does not map, so its floor cannot be computed and the required `declared_floor_ref` has no rule behind it.
why: `public-claims` is the term that floors CAP-13 at the economic/contractual class, which is what 05 section 11 states in prose. Unmapped, CAP-13's floor is uncomputable -- and that was the state of ALL 53 terms: capabilities.json had no floor field of any name and zero occurrences of any C0-C5 token, while `ConsequenceDerivation.declared_floor_ref` was required. Two implementers mapping 53 domain terms onto six classes differently decide who may act differently, and the mapping table was named three times across two chapters without existing.
expect_failure_contains: A CAPABILITY DECLARES A CONSEQUENCE TERM THE MAPPING TABLE DOES NOT MAP
